question.problem: A sample ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},{X}_{3},{X}_{4}$ of four cellphones is drawn from a population. The population has cellphones of two different screen sizes, $4.5\,\text{in}$ and $6\,\text{in},$ distributed in the ratio $4:1.$ Calculate the standard error of $\overset{―}{X}.$ Round your answer to two decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu $ and population variance ${\sigma }^{2},$ then

$$
\text{E}[\overset{―}{X}]=\mu ,\,\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]=\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n},
$$

and the standard error is given by

$$
\text{SE}[\overset{―}{X}]=\sqrt{\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]}=\frac{\sigma }{\sqrt{n}}.
$$

We're told that the cellphones in the population have screen sizes of $4.5\,\text{in}$ and $6\,\text{in},$ and these are distributed in the ratio $4:1.$ Therefore, to compute the population's mean and variance, we can consider a population consisting of $4+1=5$ cellphones only with the following screen sizes:

$$
4.5\,\text{in},\,4.5\,\text{in},\,4.5\,\text{in},\,4.5\,\text{in},\,6\,\text{in}.
$$

Therefore, the population mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu  & =\frac{1}{5}{\sum }_{i}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(4\cdot 4.5+6) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(18+6) \\  & =\frac{24}{5} \\  & =4.8\,\text{in},\end{aligned}
$$

and the population variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\frac{1}{5}{\sum }_{i}{x}_{i}^{2}-{\mu }^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(4\cdot {4.5}^{2}+{6}^{2})-{4.8}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(117)-23.04 \\  & =23.4-23.04 \\  & =0.36\,{\text{in}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the sample size is $n=4,$ we have

$$
\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]=\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}=\frac{0.36}{4}=0.09\,{\text{in}}^{2}.
$$

Finally,

$$
\text{SE}[\overset{―}{X}]=\sqrt{0.09}=0.3\,\text{in}.
$$
